l.i: mine religiosè illo utedum,ad Deigloriam, & subiectorum emendationem & incolumitatem. Deus Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi,& ipsum & uos perpetuo sanctifi-cet per ueritatem suam: nec unquam uersutia Satanæ circumueniri,aut a laudabi-li uera tum pietatis, tum uirtutis studio abduci,patiatur.

main_text.l: Mirifice delector Anacharsis Philosophi Epistola ad Lydorum Rege Croesum, in qua, cur Aulica uita,ad quà humanissimè inuitabatur, Academicum puluere sibi præferre dum iudicârit,rationes his uerbis exponit: Ego, Lydorum Rex, in Graciam profectus sum, Graecorum mores, studia atq; instituta percepturus. Auro autem non egeo:satisq; mihi est, si ad meos Scythas redeam MELIOR & DOCTIOR. Veniam tamen ad te Sardis, plurimi faciens tibi familiarem & amicum fieri.
Si homo Ethnicus,nõ solum ut DOCTI-OR.sed etiâ ut MELIOR fieret,sibi & peregrinandū in Gracia,& summo studio elaborandū censuit: quàto magis nos omnes, qui in Christū Iesum nos credere ꝓfitemur,

page.notes: Long s is printed as f in the scan and is transcribed as s. "ꝓfitemur" is doubtful: the abbreviation mark is hard to read, so it is marked [?]-equivalent in this notes field; the reading "profitemur" is likely. "Regè", "quà", "humanissimè" and "quàto" carry grave or circumflex marks that are hard to make out and may be misread. "Gracia" and "Graciam" are read as printed. The catchword "totis" is taken from the sentence's continuation on the next page.
